attacks.claim: `.day-card` hardcodes a white background while its text uses `var(--text)`, which becomes near-white (#f2f2f7) under dark mode. About 30% of users run dark mode, so the card text is nearly unreadable for them at full rollout. The muted meta text (#a1a1a6 on white) is also roughly 2.4:1, below WCAG AA. The defect is reversible via the flag, so major rather than blocker.
attacks.evidence: ".day-card { background: #ffffff; color: var(--text); ... }" with "--text: #f2f2f7" and "--surface: #1c1c1e" under prefers-color-scheme: dark; QA: "Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass"

attacks.claim: The 72px fixed mobile action bar has no matching bottom padding or spacer on `.planner` or body, so the last day (Sunday) and its tiles, and any focused control scrolled to the bottom, can sit under the bar. No iOS safe-area inset is specified either. No QA covers scrolling to the end of the planner.
attacks.evidence: ".action-bar { position: fixed; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 72px; ... }" with ".planner { ... padding: 16px; ... }" and no bottom padding; "Sunday is the last child of .planner"; ABSENT: scroll-padding, bottom spacer, or scroll-to-end QA

attacks.claim: The one-tap "+ List" button, which serves the most frequent planner action (9.4 adds per WAU per week, 64% on mobile), is removed. Adding one recipe now takes about five to six steps. The only bulk shortcut adds the whole week, so it does not replace per-recipe adds. The stated decluttering goal does not justify this, and no usability test, timing data, or A/B result supports the change.
attacks.evidence: "The old tile-level \"+ List\" button is removed to declutter tiles." vs "tap the tile → recipe page → \"Ingredients\" tab → choose servings … → \"Add to list\" → toast with \"Undo\""; ABSENT: usability test, task-completion timing, or funnel comparison

attacks.claim: QA covers only light mode, on desktop Chrome at 1440px and iPhone 14 Safari. It does not cover dark mode, the 360px low end of the 360–414px mobile range, or touch-drag. Since 68% of sessions are mobile and about 30% use dark mode, the dark-mode defect above would have been caught by a dark-mode pass.
attacks.evidence: "Visual QA vs Figma: Chrome 1440px (light), Safari iPhone 14 (light) — pass, pixel diffs < 1%." vs "68% of sessions are on mobile (360-414px wide)"; ABSENT: dark-mode or 360px evidence

attacks.claim: The flow says "tap the tile → recipe page", but the abbreviated markup shows no link or button wrapping the tile or title, so keyboard and screen-reader users may have no obvious way to open a recipe. The markup is abbreviated, so this may be handled in code not shown; confirm before ship.
attacks.evidence:
`

  • Sheet-pan gnocchi

    25 min

    ...` (no anchor or role on tile); "Markup (`planner.html`, abbreviated)"

attacks.claim: Every tile's "Swap" button has the same label with no recipe-specific aria-label, so a screen-reader user cannot tell which recipe each one swaps. Only the overflow button has a recipe-specific label.
attacks.evidence: `<button class="btn-ghost">Swap</button>` vs `<button class="btn-icon" aria-label="More options for Sheet-pan gnocchi">`

attacks.claim: The toast and the "Generate shopping list" result are not specified as live-region announcements, so screen-reader users may not learn that an add succeeded.
attacks.evidence: "toast with 'Undo'"; ABSENT: aria-live or role=status specification

attacks.claim: "Generate shopping list" adds all planned recipes in one tap, with no confirmation, preview, or stated undo. Repeated taps or an existing list could create duplicate line items, and an accidental tap is hard to review. The label also does not make the week-wide scope clear.
attacks.evidence: "New sticky bottom bar on mobile with \"Generate shopping list\" (adds all planned recipes for the week)"; ABSENT: confirmation, undo, or duplicate-handling behavior

attacks.claim: The dark-mode border on the action bar is `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` on a black page, so the bar edge is nearly invisible and not visually separated from the content.
attacks.evidence: "border-top: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.08);" with "--page: #000000" in dark mode

attacks.claim: The bar's two 48px-min-height buttons have no width, flex, or wrapping rules, so the "Generate shopping list" label may wrap or crowd "Share plan" at 360px.
attacks.evidence: ".action-bar { ... display: flex; gap: 12px; }" and ".btn-primary { ... min-height: 48px; ... }" with no flex or width rules for the buttons

attacks.claim: The rollback is described as a flag flip with no data migration, but no test of the flag-off path is reported. Since the rollback is the safety net for a 100% ship, it should be exercised before crossing.
attacks.evidence: "old planner remains available by flipping the flag off (same API, no data migration)"; ABSENT: test of the flag-off path

attacks.claim: The watch list has no thresholds, owners, or abort criteria for JS errors, shopping-list additions per WAU, or bounce rate, so a dark-mode or layout regression has no defined stop condition during the 100% rollout.
attacks.evidence: "Watch: planner page JS errors, shopping-list additions/WAU, planner bounce rate."; ABSENT: thresholds or stop criteria

attacks.claim: The Lighthouse figures (performance 91, CLS 0.01) have no page, viewport, or current-planner baseline, so they cannot show the redesign did not regress.
attacks.evidence: "Lighthouse mobile: performance 91, accessibility 100, CLS 0.01."; ABSENT: baseline or test URL/viewport
